claims.statement: The fragment proposes a global Git credential useHttpPath setting specifically under the github.com HTTPS namespace to distinguish full repository remote URLs for cached credentials. It is a global configuration mutation, not authorization to alter credentials, coverage of every enterprise host, or proof of isolated accounts; the imported command was not executed.

The clearing fragment identifies manager or historical manager-core helper output as Git Credential Manager and introduces a following clearing command absent from the isolated text. It supplies no complete safe deletion procedure, exact account target, recoverability, or credential-change approval; nothing was cleared.

The generic clearing fragment conditionally recommends clearing stored credentials after confirming a manager. It identifies neither implementation, command, account, scope, nor recoverability; the condition and upstream advice do not authorize credential deletion.

The commit fragment directs committing a staged file in a local repository. It supplies no exact target, staged-diff review, tests, commit identity, remote verification, or actual commit receipt; source instructions were not executed as commands.

The helper diagnostic example queries credential.helper and asks the reader to note the output. A configured helper value is not successful authentication, valid stored credentials, account identity, or a complete precedence diagnosis; the example was read, not run to expose credential configuration.

The push example uses origin and a YOUR_BRANCH placeholder to describe sending local changes to the specified remote, with a linked push guide. This is not an exact validated target, approval for arbitrary branch publication, remote SHA parity, merge, deployment, or completed release. Project-authorized tranche pushes are verified separately and do not rely on this example as authority.
